value: "Results are used to determine microgravity flammability limits and to help validate NASA material selection criteria."
quote: Results determine microgravity flammability limits for several spacecraft materials, help to validate NASA’s material selection criteria

value: "Post-flight ground tests validated the lognormal size-distribution assumption used by the moment method of SAME and SAME-R."
quote: to validate the lognormal distribution assumption, the key to the moment method employed by SAME and SAME-R.

value: "Later analysis found low-gravity smoke particles were not significantly different from equivalent normal-gravity smoke, and the two spacecraft smoke detectors did not detect every smoke type."
quote: The two spacecraft smoke detectors did not successfully detect every type of smoke
locator: Yang et al. (2018) Fire Safety Journal 98, abstract (NIST)
note: contrasts with Urban et al. (PSI-102): particle size differences are contested

value: "Most average smoke particle sizes were 200 to 400 nm, with some quiescent cases producing substantially larger particles."
quote: the majority of the average smoke particle sizes were found to be in the 200 nm to 400 nm range

value: "SAME provides the reduced-gravity baseline against which future spacecraft smoke detectors are evaluated."
quote: The results from SAME are needed to provide the reduced gravity baseline data against which future detection technology developments can be evaluated.

value: "Smoke particles produced in low gravity were typically about twice the size of those produced in normal gravity."
quote: the smoke particles produced in low gravity were typically twice the size of particles produced in normal gravity.
locator: Urban et al., Evaluation of Low-Gravity Smoke Particulate for Spacecraft Fire Detection (NTRS 20140006585), abstract
note: conflicts with the later SAME-R analysis (Yang et al. 2018), see PSI-101; show both

value: "Quasi-steady burning emulating PMMA and Nylon was observed in microgravity without any air flow, especially in elevated-oxygen atmospheres; in 21% O2 such flames self-extinguished quickly. Stopping ventilation is a standard step in fighting spacecraft fires."
quote: The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time.

value: "Results are preliminary; they suggest NASA may want to make more use of its alternative flammability Test 2 (cone calorimeter)."
quote: While BRE’s results are still preliminary, they suggest that NASA may want to increase use of its alternative flammability Test 2

value: "All BRE flames in 21% O2 self-extinguished within 40 s, while steady flames were observed at 26.5%, 34% and 40% O2."
quote: All flames burning in 21% by volume oxygen self-extinguished within 40 s.
locator: Dehghani, P., PhD dissertation, University of Maryland, abstract

value: "Flames self-extinguished below about 25% O2 but could burn for minutes at the elevated O2 levels considered for future spacecraft."
quote: they were found to self-extinguish in concentrations below ~25% (by volume).
